history.dynasty: Pandya-era construction with Chola influences; inscriptions of the Cholas, Pandyas and Udayars
history.period: Believed 10th-12th century CE; some sculptures claimed to be ~5th century AD - FLAG: dates conflict between sources, verify locally
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV gives town as Tiruppur, but the temple is at Sarkar Periyapalayam (Sircar Periapalayam) on Uthukuli Road, about 8 km from Tiruppur city, on the northern bank of the Noyyal river. A Vaippu Sthalam sung by the Nayanar saint Sundarar. The temple is named Sukreeswarar because the vanara king Sugriva built a lingam here to atone for the killing of his brother Vali (Ramayana association); Indra's elephant Iravatham is also said to have worshipped here. Ancient names include Kurakkuthali (the place of the monkey worshipper) and Mukundapuri/Mukundaipuri; in inscriptions the deity is called Aludaya Pillai and Milakeesan. A protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India, built of carved stone in Pandya style with later Chola additions. Specialities: at the meeting of Dakshinayana and Uttarayana the sun's rays fall on the deity; the southern wall carries a sculpture of a monkey worshipping the lingam; two Nandis stand before the deity, one without ears (legend: a farmer cut the ear of a bull that ate his crops, then saw blood on the stone Nandi - he was cured of his family's affliction only after another Nandi was made and the earless one placed in front of the Lord by divine command). There are five lingams in all - one in the main shrine, three outside, and one in invisible (sukshma) form.

name: Sri Sukreeswarar Temple
town_description: Sarkar Periyapalayam is a village on Uthukuli Road about 8 km from Tiruppur city, in Tiruppur district, known mainly for this ancient ASI-protected Shiva temple on the ancient Kongu trade route, close to the textile hub of Tiruppur.

travel.airport: Coimbatore International Airport, about 50 km away, is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Tiruppur railway station, about 8 km away, is the nearest railhead.
travel.road: Uthukuli Road, Sircar Periapalayam, Tiruppur 641607; a short drive off the Tiruppur-Uthukuli highway.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Mahashivratri and Pradosham days draw the main crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM-1:00 PM and 5:30-8:00 PM daily (one source says morning closing at noon and evening 4:30-7:30 - verify locally). Phone: 097880 61237.
